Title:YANG DI-PERTUAN NEGARA'S SPEECH (Debate on the Address)
MPs Speaking:Dr Toh Chin Chye (Deputy Prime Minister and Leader of the House); Mr Jek Yeun Thong (Minister for Labour); Mr Lee Kuan Yew (Prime Minister); Mr Ong Pang Boon (Minister for Education); Mr Yong Nyuk Lin (Minister for Health); Mr Bernard Rodrigues; Mr Chia Thye Poh; Mr Ho See Beng; Mr Koo Young; Mr Poh Ber Liak; Mr Sim Boon Woo; Mr E. W. Barker (Mr Speaker);




YANG DI-PERTUAN NEGARA'S SPEECH

(Debate on the Address)


2.43 p.m.

    The Minister for Labour (Mr Jek Yeun Thong)(In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, Sir, the amendment moved by the Barisan Sosialis means that they are crying, "Catch the thief", when they themselves are thieves, as a Chinese story goes. They themselves have caused this situation of confrontation between Malaysia and Indonesia. Now they want to shift the blame on to the shoulders of others. They are blaming others as the culprits in order to clear their own names. Their action is really very wonderful and fantastic.

    We should review what has taken place in the past few years. It is now the time for stock-taking. Let us now review our achievements in the past few years we have been in office. Singapore is a paradise in South-East Asia. Our people, irrespective of race and class, are enjoying a livelihood and standard of living much better than that of any other country in South-East Asia. Had it not been for the agitation and instigation of the Barisan Sosialis which has brought about confrontation against Malaysia, our Malaysia and Singapore especially would have achieved unprecedented prosperity and happiness. But because of the stupidity and stubbornness of the Barisan Sosialis in persisting in their line of confrontation, we have now amongst us thousands of poor labourers who have to pay the price of the Barisan misdeeds.

    Let us ask, which country in South-East Asia is enjoying the same high standard of living which we are enjoying? Which country in this part of the world has been enjoying the same standard of living, or whose people are better clothed, better fed and have better enjoyment? Just look around those

Column: 171

countries, such as Indonesia. The people there are in deep water and in great difficulties. They cannot enjoy what we are now enjoying. They have even difficulty in filling their stomachs. They are now even eating roots, the bark of trees and fruits to fill their stomachs. Perhaps they could explain their way and say, as the Indonesian leaders have said, that the spirit of revolution can resolve all this, and that the people should put the revolutionary spirit first before the satisfaction of their hunger. But in asking their people to tighten their belts, these so-called leaders are driving their people to starvation. It is fortunate that we have no such leadership in our State. Otherwise we would be suffering the same kind of misfortune as they are now suffering. In which country are the people enjoying the same standard of living as we are enjoying here? Our currency is the strongest and most stable in South-East Asia. For example, if the $500 allowance given to the Barisan Members is put into a bank. they can still buy $500 worth of goods when they draw it out next month.

    Let us see the situation in Indonesia today. It is unimaginable. Even the Japanese banana notes or coconut notes are worth more than the Indonesian currency nowadays. If a Nanyang University lecturer in Mathematics were to calculate the Indonesian currency, he would have to calculate it in five or six digits, as the Indonesian children are learning in their schools. Under such tuition perhaps the Barisan Members could have better enlightenment. For instance, in 1960 Mr Chan Sun Wing followed the Prime Minister to Indonesia on a friendly visit, and he carried two bags full of Indonesian currency in order to buy goods. He was looking for goods everywhere, and he had to carry such a bundle of Indonesian notes with him. This is the situation with regard to the Indonesian currency and economy. Inflation is rampant and there are economic difficulties.

    Here in Singapore we have schools. We have a place in school for every child, to whatever school the child wants to go, whether it is Tamil, Malay or English. The children of Singapore can

Column: 172

go to any school in any part of Singapore, in the South Bridge Road area or in the North Bridge Road area or in Queenstown. Here we have free primary education. Students who are poor but diligent can get bursaries and scholarships. I believe that among the Nanyang University friends of the Barisan there are many students who have Government scholarships and bursaries to go for higher studies. They can make use of Government scholarships to continue their studies in secondary schools and the universities. Let me ask, in which country in South-East Asia are such facilities afforded to the people?

    Here among us we also have cheap housing. The Government is giving subsidies for the people to have their accommodation. The people can choose to live in the North Bridge Road area or the South Bridge Road area or anywhere in Singapore. They can also choose to have one-room, two-room or three-room flats. They have this right to make a choice. It is not any country in South-East Asia which has this kind of facilities, even in the whole world there are very few countries which can afford these facilities to the people. If the people fall sick, there are doctors to prescribe for them and they do not have to pay a single cent for this service. The Government is providing clinics which are right at your doorstep and poor children can get a free milk supply. Let me ask, how many countries in the whole world can afford these medical services and other free facilities to the people?

    Our workers are enjoying a standard of wages and living far better than anywhere in South-East Asia.

    In our Yang di-Pertuan Negara's speech it is also disclosed that the number of vehicles registered this year has increased by 45 per cent more than that of last year. Now, this figure can very aptly be taken to show the raising of the living standard of the workers. We have progressive labour legislation which will protect the workers' interests, and the Industrial Relations ordinance provides for good relationships between the employer and the employee. Very few

Column: 173

countries in South-East Asia can have such enlightened legislation for the benefit of the workers.

    All people, irrespective of their situation, can get aid from the Government. Every year we are spending millions of dollars on public assistance, such as fire relief funds, unemployment assistance and other schemes of aid. Ours is a socialist welfare state policy. The rich are sharing their wealth with the poor, and this is only just and reasonable. Our society is marching towards this type of socialist society. Who can say that we do not have socialist legislation? These opportunities of employment and the provision of the facilities I have stated above are for all the people to enjoy irrespective of whether they are against or for the P.A.P. - even among Members of the Barisan who are enjoying our low-cost housing facilities. We are so used to seeing these favourable conditions and facilities that we sometimes forget about the value of these facilities. It is just as what we say, being amongst the flowers for so long, one forgets their fragrance. In fact, we tend to think that we get these things as our natural right, which other countries can never dream to have. We should thank our Yang di-Pertuan Negara for his speech which affords us an opportunity to remind all our people that we are living in a very healthy and fortunate country.

    After the establishment of Malaysia as the New York of Malaysia, we can expect that we can further raise the standard of living of our people. We have all the factors and conditions to fulfil this. We have further reason to believe that we can even bring about more wealth and enjoyment to the people. We have a very good and efficient administration, communication, fiscal and trade systems. After Malaysia, our goods will have a larger market and will also be protected by tariff legislation. We will also have rich material resources. All this will bring about a better future for us. These are the main factors that will bring this about. We are now on the road to prosperity, happiness and a better future.

Column: 174



    But we are now facing Indonesian confrontation which has caused thousands of people to be out of job and a depression in our trade. Who has caused all this? Who has disturbed the beautiful dream of our people? To go to the root of the matter, we can say that the confrontation policy by Indonesia today is caused by the Barisan Sosialis. They are the culprits. The Barisan Members should know that the unemployment of thousands of our workers today and the depression in our trade are, to a certain extent, caused by them. They should be responsible for all these consequences because they have tried their best to oppose Malaysia and do all things possible to destroy our democratic system and affluent society. When we want to lay hands on any culprit, we should lay it on the Barisan Members. It is they who have caused us these difficulties - the unemployment of thousands of our workers and depression in our trade. They are the arch-culprits who have caused this trouble arising from the Indonesian confrontation policy. We can see very well that at the beginning of this two-year struggle for Malaysia, Indonesia had not opposed Malaysia. Even Dr Subandrio in December 1962 said in New York that Indonesia was not against Malaysia, if it was the wish of the people. On the other hand, Indonesia would give Malaysia her blessing. At that time the Barisan's opposition to Malaysia throughout Malaysia had not the support of the people and the referendum held in September had also dealt the Barisan a deadly crushing blow. Later they changed their strategy and secured the support of the Indonesian leaders, especially the P.K.I., to provide them with spiritual and moral support in their opposition to Malaysia. The P.K.I. passed a resolution last year condemning Malaysia. At that time the Barisan were very elated. The resolution passed by the P.K.I. gave them a stimulant to continue their activities against Malaysia. They took heart from that resolution and persisted in their opposition to Malaysia. Now we cannot deny that the Indonesian confrontation against Malaysia has been instigated

Column: 175

and encouraged by the Barisan Sosialis. Even the Barisan themselves last year admitted this. We could use their own documents and publications to prove this point. In the issue of the Chinese organ of the Barisan Sosialis of the 1st of December, on the second page, there was published an article the subject of which was "The Cause of Malayan Socialist Front in the Present Situation"; of course, this includes the Singapore Barisan. The first part of the article says --- [Interruption]. How can you say that I am talking at random? This is from your own article, published by your own Party. It is from your own Party organ printed in black and white. How can you say that I am quoting at random? Now let me quote:

    "First it must be pointed out that the Barisan was the first who opposed the Malaysia Plan in 1961. At that time, Indonesia did not express their opposition to the Malaysia Plan. The P.K.I. elements and other people started to oppose the Malaysia Plan only after we had done so ---"

    [Interruption] Now, this is what you say in your own article. I am not arguing who is leading whom. Please listen to the end.

    "At that time, Indonesia did not express their opposition to the Malaysia Plan. The P.K.I. elements and other people started to oppose the Malaysia Plan only after we had done so. Therefore, if there was anybody following anybody's line, then it must be they who follow our line and not we who follow their line. We challenge anybody to rebut this fact." ---

    [Interruption] This is what you yourselves have said, or your friends have said. Now, this is making your own confession without being asked to do so. Only this will go to prove that had it not been for the Barisan's instigation and encouragement and trouble making, Indonesia would not have started a confrontation for no reason at all.

    In the article it is stated "Malayan Socialist Front" but we know that Singapore's Barisan Sosialis and the Malayan Socialist Front are birds of the same feather. They themselves have admitted that the Indonesian confrontation against Malaysia is following their line. Even the Barisan Sosialis and the Socialist Front in Malaya have admitted

Column: 176

this. Now, who can say no? The reasons for Indonesian confrontation against Malaysia are partly due to her own internal economic difficulties. This can serve as a red herring to divert the attention of the people as well as foreign countries to her internal difficulties and economic disaster. On the other hand, it is because the big shots in Indonesia have also taken cognisance of the fact that the Barisan's subversive activities in Singapore will provide them with a golden opportunity to divide our people and swallow up North Borneo through the Barisan here. But the people in Indonesia have forgotten that the people of Malaysia in this crisis have all united together to deliver a crushing blow to the Barisan. Indonesia wants to make use of this opportunity to swallow up the Borneo territories. This is her true intention.

    As for the pretext that Malaysia is a threat to the security of Indonesia - it is all humbug. The so-called military base, neo-colonialism, and the rest, are all pretexts used by these people, including the Barisan Sosialis. Yet the Barisan are supporting them on this specious pretext. Can they not see that Malaysia, without any airplanes or warships, cannot be a threat to the security of Indonesia, a country which has so much armoury and such a great army? We can see that when the Yang di-Pertuan Agong visited Singapore, he came in a very small light out-moded military plane. We do not even have an air force but Indonesia has a large fleet of jet planes. The Indonesian President, Dr Soekarno, has his own special jet plane to fly him about. And Indonesia has warships, arms and submarines, supplied by Russia as well as America. But we do not have these. So how can we be a threat to others?

    The military base in Malaysia has been in existence even before the Indonesian revolution and independence. Why did they then not object to it? Why should they wait till after Malaysia has been established to protest against the existence of this base?

Column: 177



    In their amendment the Barisan Sosialis urges the Government to persuade the Central Government to get rid of foreign interference and to ask for the abolition of the British military base. But if we abolish the base today, tomorrow it will be an Indonesian colony, and our livelihood and living standard will be worse than that under the Japanese regime, not to talk of the thousands of Naval Base workers who will be out of job.

    We can recollect that Indonesia first opposed Malaysia after December 1962 when Azahari's rebellion in Brunei took place. During that period Indonesia had been encouraging a rebellion. Before the Brunei rebellion the rebel leader Azahari had flown into Singapore to have talks with Barisan leaders, including Lim Ching Siong. After the rebellion in Brunei the Barisan Sosialis came out to give full support to the rebellion and to the self-styled revolutionist hiding in a hotel in Manila, and they termed him a hero of the liberation of Brunei. Yet they failed disastrously.

    Brunei is an oil producing country, a rich country, and the people do not have taxes like income tax, cigarette tax, oil tax, and other taxes. What reason do they have to rebel against authority? And now Azahari has fled to Indonesia to become a stooge of Dr Subandrio and to be used as an exhibit at mass rallies.

    This a very clear example of their collaboration and collusion with a foreign enemy to destroy our country. I recall that at the Afro-Asian Conference at Moshi last year the Indonesian delegates tried to bar our delegates from entering the conference room. Yet they were very concerned about the Barisan delegate. Mr Lim Shee Ping, because Mr Lim Shee Ping was detained during his journey and could not attend the conference. They were very worried and concerned. They asked us, "Why is it that a partner of yours has not turned up?" In fact, at that time we did not know that Mr Lim Shee Ping had been

Column: 178

detained. When the Indonesian delegates knew that Mr Lim Shee Ping could not attend the conference, they mobilised all their efforts to lobby all the delegates to prevent us from participating in the conference. And at the sub-committee meeting the anti-Malaysian forces were able to gain an overwhelming control over the meeting.

    From this we can see that before the conference the fanatics against Malaysia must have established contact through correspondence and they must have tried to make use of the Barisan delegate to be the main mouthpiece at the Afro-Asian Conference against Malaysia. Because Mr Lim Shee Ping could not turn up, they had no alternative but to use two so-called delegates from Indonesia to represent the Barisan delegates. This is another example of the Barisan's collusion with the foreign enemy.

    Our present difficult economic situation was brought about by them, and yet they have the cheek to put in an amendment blaming us for causing difficulties to the people as a result of Malaysia. Without the Barisan Sosialis, we the people of Malaysia will be the happiest people in South-East Asia, but because of them we have a lot of difficulties and hardships and so much disturbance.

    I know that in their amendment the Barisan Sosialis also mention the false imposition of Malaysia on the people. What do they mean by imposition? We do not have to talk about Sabah and Sarawak. Let us talk about Singapore. Within a year there have been two occasions for the people to vote on the question whether they like Malaysia or not. That was on the 1st September, 1962. On that day more than 70 per cent of the people voted for Malaysia and rejected their blank vote suggestion. Although the voting was compulsory, there were three choices, and they freely accepted Malaysia. Are not the people's eyes very clear? The second occasion was in September this year - the general elections. We put forward Malaysia as one of our Party platforms and as a result of that we won a great

Column: l79

majority. Whether it was a snap election or not, they had nine days to campaign. And in all this time they had consistently and persistently carried out their anti-Malaysia campaign for two and a half years. Yet they were defeated. Now in those general elections, the Barisan Sosialis put forward anti-Malaysia as their election platform. What was the outcome? They had only 13 seats, an unlucky number. And today among them one has disappeared, their Party leader, Dr Lee Siew Choh. And their three other Members have also disappeared from this House. Where are they now?

    Mr Speaker: Order. It is five o'clock. I propose to suspend this sitting. I will take this Chair again at 5.30 p.m.

Sitting accordingly suspended
at 5 p.m. until 5.30 p.m.


Sitting resumed at 5.30 p.m.

[Mr Speaker in the Chair]



    Debate resumed.

    Mr Speaker: The Minister for Labour had the Floor.

    Mr Jek Yeun Thong(In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, before the break, I was saying that the Barisan Sosialis in the recent general elections used anti-Malaysia policy as one of their platforms. As a result, they have secured only thirteen Assembly seats - the unlucky number of thirteen! Today, we have seen even the Member for Bukit Merah is not here. Perhaps there is another crisis in the Barisan.

    What I want to say is that the recent general elections were conducted in a most free and democratic way. Those who are for Malaysia voted for our candidates; those who are against Malaysia voted for Barisan candidates. How can you say that anybody has imposed Malaysia on the people? If the logic of the Barisan were correct that Malaysia had been imposed on the people, then we the Members of this House would also be an imposition on

Column: 180

the people, including the Barisan Members. Whether they have made their Assembly seats a kind of imposition on the people is another matter. If they admit it, then their seats are a kind of imposition on the people, and they should vacate them. But I will say that the people voted for Malaysia by a free and democratic process.

    The Member for Jurong mentioned the question of the four streams of education. On the question of Chinese education, the Barisan slogans are usually like this, that we want to destroy Chinese education. Now, what do they know about the destruction of Chinese education? What do they mean? Take, for instance, Thailand, the Philippines and Indonesia. What about the attitude of the Government in these countries against Chinese schools? Now, this is a real example of attempts to destroy Chinese education. But, here in Singapore, is the P.A.P. Government trying to destroy Chinese education? On what grounds do they raise these groundless accusations?

    You, Members of the Barisan, are or educated purely in Chinese. Now, please think of the time when you were educated in Chinese schools. What was the situation then, and what is the situation today? Would you please compare the two situations? If the Barisan Members have a conscience, they should admit that Chinese education nowadays is very much better than it was before. Nowadays it is not necessary to mention the time when they were educated in Chinese schools.

    I will just give an example in my case. My parents had to save money to send me and people of my generation to primary schools. But nowadays, just look at the present Chinese primary schools. The children do not have to pay for anything. If it was not for the confrontation policy of Indonesia, we would have achieved free secondary education. Those children whose families are poor can be provided with free textbooks by the Government. Now, please consider this. Do you think this

Column: 181

is the way to destroy Chinese education? I would say that this is a concrete example to show that Chinese education nowadays is enjoying much better facilities than before.

    In the past, if you wanted to join a school, you would have to ask people to recommend you, to persuade perhaps the principals or teachers in certain schools to let you have a place in school. But just look around now. Now, the children do not have to do such things. They have no fear of not getting a place in school. Any child wishing to join any school, whether a Tamil, or a Malay, or an English or a Chinese school, would be given a place in a school nearest to his or her home. This is a second point to show how much better Chinese education is treated nowadays than it was in the past.

    Another point is, in the past, teachers in Chinese schools would have to try to make blandishments to those on top who had control of the schools in order to retain their position. On top of this, their salaries were not stable, or rather, in the primary schools the salaries were determined by the principals who could impose their will. Sometimes teachers did not get their salaries at all.

    I can recall an example of my old friend, Mr Leong Keng Seng of the Barisan Sosialis, when he was principal for the first time in 1955. At that time we were still friends. When he received his salary he used to ask me to go for a drive with him to have dinner together. But sometimes when it was time for him to give me a treat, he did not do so. For what reason? It was because he had not received the salary due to him at the right time, so he had no money to give me a treat, because the primary school in which he was teaching would have to wait for the school fees to be paid by the pupils before the school could issue salaries to the teachers. In the rural areas, in the kampongs, if the pupils of a school could not afford to pay their school fees, then the school would have to delay the payment of salaries to the teachers, and the teachers would have

Column: 182

to tighten their belts! But now the situation is entirely different. Now, the payment of salaries to the teachers does not depend on the school fees paid by the pupils, because the whole burden is on the Government. The teachers also have definite salary scales, annual increments and other benefits. They get their salary on time regularly, and they are well treated. Those teachers who have taught for more than ten years can get quarters or buy cars for themselves. Our old friend, Mr Leong Keng Seng, after having been a school principal for a few years, would at least have enough money to buy a car ---
